newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar opens firmer in light trading.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar opens firmer in light trading.

text.p: The Canadian dollar opened slightly firmer at C$1.3921 (US$0.7183) in light trading on Thursday after a quiet night on overseas markets, traders said.

They said the decline of the Canada dollar in afternoon trading on Wednesday had little to do with comments by Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen who said the central bank had some room to maneuver if the U.S. hiked interest rates.
Thiessen told reporters following a speech in Quebec City that Canada's improved fiscal position had helped provide the Bank of Canada with more flexibility.

Some people interpreted the comments as a market-mover, but there were technical reasons behind the sell-off of the Canadian dollar, said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC Wood Gundy.

"It didn't move because of what Thiessen said," Farrill said. "The flows started long before he (Thiessen) began to speak. Stops were triggered at C$1.3885 (US$0.7194), then the options came in and that was it."
Analysts said they expected a quieter trading session for the Canadian dollar, though the release of merchandise trade data this morning would put a damper on any dollar rallies.

Statistics Canada reported that Canada's trade surplus shrank to C$1.7 billion in April from a revised C$2.6 billion in March. The agency said exports increased to C$24.6 billion from C$24.5 billion in March and imports rose to C$22.8 billion from C$21.9 billion.
A Reuters forecast of economists had forecast a surplus of C$2.9 billion in April, with exports of C$23.9 billion and imports of C$20.6 billion.
"The trade surplus is a lot lower than we expected which is going to bring up current account concerns," said Steve Saldanha, economist with Canada Trust Investment Management.
"We will probably have another negative in the current account, which will have a slight negative bias for the (Canada) dollar," Saldanha said.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar rose to 81.80 yen from Wednesday's 81.48 yen and climbed to 1.2454 marks from Wednesday's 1.2431 marks.
